headline: The Catholic Ministry Foundation
threshold: By Lesson 10, you can greet parishioners, give Mass times and dates, say what a family needs for a sacrament, ask simple questions, make polite requests, and start Catholic Ministry Lesson 1.

lessons.title: Sounds and Greetings
lessons.objective: Pronounce key church words and greet parishioners at the door before and after Mass.
lessons.focus: The five vowels, ch, j, ll, rr and the written accent; greetings

words.note: Each vowel is short and clear: ee-GLEH-syah.
Pure vowels, no glide: MEE-sah.
Address a priest directly as padre.
ll sounds like English y: kah-PEE-yah.
An r at the start of a word is trilled like rr.
The written accent marks the stress: o-rah-SYOHN.
j sounds like a strong English h: EE-ho.
ch sounds as in English church.
rr is a strong rolled trill: en-TYEH-rro.
Stress the accented syllable: DYAH-ko-no.

words.en: Good morning, my name is Miguel.
I work here at the parish.

words.note: Formal; use it with parishioners you don't know well.
Say lo to a man, la to a woman, los to a group.

lessons.speaking: Greet a parishioner at the church door, say your name and that you work at the parish, and wish them God's blessing.

lessons.title: Numbers, Time and Measurements
lessons.objective: Give Mass times, page numbers, counts and prices for parish events.
lessons.focus: Numbers 0 to 1,000, clock time (a las 12:30), and counts of pages, minutes, people and dollars

words.note: Los domingos means on Sundays, every week.
A las 9 de la mañana means at 9 a.m.
A las 5 de la tarde means at 5 p.m.

words.es: La misa en español es a las 12:30.
words.note: Use a las for at with clock times.

words.es: Abran el cancionero en la página 125.
words.note: Ustedes command to the whole congregation.

words.en: The retreat costs 25 dollars per person.
words.es: El retiro cuesta 25 dólares por persona.

lessons.speaking: Tell a visitor what time the Spanish Mass is, how long the class lasts, and what page to open in the hymnal.

lessons.title: Ser and Estar
lessons.objective: Describe people, places and conditions in the parish with ser and estar.
lessons.focus: ser for what something or someone is, estar for its condition or location

words.note: Agrees with the noun: la iglesia está abierta.
Use estar for a feeling right now: está triste.
Ser for identity: es católico, es católica.

words.es: La iglesia está abierta hasta las 6.
words.note: estar: a condition that can change.

words.es: El padre está en la sacristía.
words.note: estar for location.

words.es: Es una parroquia grande y bilingüe.
words.note: ser: what something is.
Say nueva to a woman.

lessons.speaking: Tell a visitor whether the church is open, where the priest is, and what kind of parish it is.

lessons.title: Have, There Is, Need and Want
lessons.objective: Say what a family has, needs and wants for a baptism, and what they have to do.
lessons.focus: tener, hay, necesitar, querer, and hay que + infinitive for documents and steps

words.note: Feminine noun that takes el in the singular: el acta, las actas.
Feminine; takes el in the singular: el agua bendita.
In Mexican parishes, la plática is the required preparation talk.

words.en: Do you have the baptism certificate?
I need the child's birth certificate.
words.es: Necesito el acta de nacimiento del niño.

words.en: Do you want to baptize your daughter?
words.note: Personal a before a person: bautizar a su hija.

words.en: There's religious education class on Sundays.
words.es: Hay clase de catequesis los domingos.

words.en: You have to fill out this form.
words.note: Hay que + infinitive: something everyone has to do.

words.en: The godparents have to go to a prep talk.
words.es: Los padrinos tienen que ir a una plática.

lessons.speaking: Tell a parent what documents they need for the baptism, ask if they have a godfather and godmother, and say what they have to do.

lessons.title: Go, Do and Can
lessons.objective: Talk about where you are going, what you plan to do, and what you can do in ministry.
lessons.focus: ir, ir a + infinitive for plans, hacer, and poder (puedo, puede)

words.note: The h is silent: os-pee-TAHL.
The celebration is los quince años; la quinceañera is the girl.

words.en: I'm going to visit your mother in the hospital.
words.es: Voy a visitar a su mamá en el hospital.
words.note: Personal a before a person: visitar a su mamá.

words.en: We're going to have the rehearsal on Friday.
words.es: Vamos a hacer el ensayo el viernes.

words.en: Are you going to have a party after the baptism?
words.es: ¿Van a hacer una fiesta después del bautizo?
words.note: El bautizo is the event; el bautismo is the sacrament.

words.en: I can bring Communion to your home.
words.es: Puedo llevar la comunión a su casa.

words.en: I can't go to the meeting tomorrow.
words.es: No puedo ir a la reunión mañana.

lessons.speaking: Tell a family when you are going to visit, what you are going to do at the rehearsal, and what you can bring.

lessons.title: Present Tense
lessons.objective: Say what you, volunteers and families regularly do at Mass and in parish groups.
lessons.focus: Present tense of -ar, -er, -ir verbs: rezo, cantas, vive, rezamos, asisten

words.note: For a woman: la lectora.
Same form for a man: el catequista.

words.en: Do you sing in the choir?
words.note: Tú is informal: use it with a fellow volunteer you know well.

words.en: You live near the church, right?
words.es: Usted vive cerca de la iglesia, ¿verdad?

words.en: We pray the rosary on Tuesdays.
words.es: Nosotros rezamos el rosario los martes.
Ellos asisten a misa cada domingo.

words.en: The children learn the prayers in religious education.
words.es: Los niños aprenden las oraciones en catequesis.

lessons.speaking: Tell a new lector what you read, what the choir sings, and when your prayer group prays the rosary.

lessons.title: Questions
lessons.objective: Ask parishioners and visitors simple questions about names, times, places and reasons.
lessons.focus: Question words qué, quién, dónde, cuándo, cuánto, cómo, por qué, cuál

words.note: Plural for more than one person: ¿quiénes?
Use ¿cuántos? for how many: ¿cuántos niños?
Two words with an accent; porque, one word, means because.
Use ¿cuál es...? for a name, number or date.

words.en: Why do you want to become Catholic?
words.note: Say católica to a woman.

lessons.speaking: Ask a newcomer their name, their phone number, when they can come to the parish office, and why they want to become Catholic.

lessons.title: No, Never and How Much
lessons.objective: Say what is missing, not done yet, or needed in larger or smaller amounts at the parish.
lessons.focus: no, nunca, nadie, nada, todavía no, más, menos, otro; double negatives (no hay nadie)

words.note: After a verb, use no first: no hay nadie.
After a verb, use no first: no tiene nada.
Never put un before it: otra misa, not una otra misa.

words.en: There's no one in the chapel.
words.es: No hay nadie en la capilla.

words.en: It's never too late to come back to the Church.
words.es: Nunca es tarde para regresar a la Iglesia.
words.note: Capital I for the Church as a community; small i for a building.

words.en: We don't have the baptism date yet.
words.es: Todavía no tenemos la fecha del bautizo.

words.en: We need more hosts for the 11 o'clock Mass.
words.es: Necesitamos más hostias para la misa de las 11.

words.en: You don't have to pay anything.
There's another Mass at 5 in the afternoon.
words.es: Hay otra misa a las 5 de la tarde.

lessons.speaking: Tell the sacristan that no one is in the chapel yet, that you need more hosts, and that there is another Mass at 5.

lessons.title: Polite Requests and Commands
lessons.objective: Ask politely and give simple usted and ustedes commands at the door, office and Mass.
lessons.focus: ¿Puede…? requests and usted commands (pase, escriba, espere); ustedes for a group

words.en: Can you open the door, please?
Come in and have a seat, please.
words.note: Usted commands for one person you address formally.

words.en: Can you give me your phone number?

words.note: Ustedes command to the whole congregation.

lessons.speaking: Welcome a visitor to the parish office: ask them politely to come in, sit down, write their full name, and wait a moment.

lessons.title: Words You Already Know and Getting Help
lessons.objective: Recognize church cognates and ask for help when you don't understand a parishioner.
lessons.focus: Cognates ending in -ción, -dad and -ente, and survival phrases for getting help

words.note: Words ending in -dad are feminine and often match English -ty.
Words ending in -ción are feminine and often match English -tion.
For a girl: la adolescente.
For a woman: la paciente.

words.en: Can you repeat that for me, please?
How do you say this in Spanish?
One moment, I'm going to call the secretary.
words.es: Un momento, voy a llamar a la secretaria.
words.note: Personal a before a person: llamar a la secretaria.

lessons.speaking: Ask a parishioner to speak more slowly and repeat, then use a few cognates to talk about the parish community and its celebrations.
